title: The lift, the orchard, the horse

breakdown.title: The lift, the orchard, the horse
breakdown.logline: In a too-small brass lift that climbs too long, a childhood friend becomes a child again unnoticed; then the door opens onto a dusk orchard of glowing apples where a white horse lowers its head to be touched.

colours.value: brass and gold in the lift; deep greens and soft warm lamp-glow from the apples at dusk; white of the horse

light.value: dim inside the lift, then warm dusk light under the trees, apples glowing softly like lamps

texture.value: brass walls and folding metal gate; smooth warm horse nose; rows of apple trees

breakdown.world_logic: A modern adult returns to an old hotel lift with a school friend. The lift climbs far too long, and without remark the friend becomes a ten-year-old in school uniform, then later is simply gone. The lift door opens directly onto an orchard at dusk where apples glow like lamps and a white horse stands still and lowers its head for the dreamer's touch.

words: had a weird one last night actually. still can’t shake it.
I was in this old hotel, in a tiny lift with brass walls and a folding metal gate. going up with my best friend from school, Tomas. we were adults.

exactly. it felt too small, and the lift just kept going up for way too long. then when I looked at Tomas again, he was about ten years old, in our old school uniform. didn’t seem to notice anything was off.
yeah. he was just sitting there like it was normal. that part’s still creepy to me.
no, I don’t think I said anything. I just stared, then the lift stopped and the gate opened.
it wasn’t a corridor or anything. it opened onto an orchard at dusk. rows of apple trees, and every apple glowing softly like a lamp.
yeah I stepped out. Tomas ran ahead between the trees, and there was a white horse standing in the middle of the orchard, very still.
I don’t remember exactly how the light hit it. just that everything felt warm and quiet and the horse was so still.
totally different. the lift was tense, but the orchard felt calm. the horse lowered its head so I could touch its nose. it was warm.
the horse, I think. that moment of touching its nose. then Tomas was gone and I woke up.
you got it right. no, you didn’t miss anything.
yes, I’d like that.
the faded watercolour one. like a memory through glass.
matches how it felt. keep the dim light.
however you imagine me is fine.
just saw them. the horse looks right, and the orchard with the apples. the lift’s too bright in the drawing, I think—I remember it being dimmer.
better. that’s more like it.
yeah, that’s it.
okay.
just took a look. looks right to me.
sounds good.
yeah, that’s right. especially the uniform.
close. I didn’t see myself stepping all the way out, I just remember being in the orchard. but Tomas running ahead is right.
perfect, thanks.
yes, that one's right.
that’s the one that matters most. looks right.
okay.
yeah. quiet and empty like that. fits.
